subject: discrete
title: Intersection of sets
prompt: Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}. What is A ∩ B?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An intersection contains exactly the elements present in both sets: 3 and 4.

subject: discrete
title: Counting a union
prompt: If |A| = 8, |B| = 7 and |A ∩ B| = 3, what is |A ∪ B|?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Inclusion–exclusion gives 8 + 7 − 3 = 12.

subject: discrete
title: A power set
prompt: How many elements are in the power set of {a, b, c}?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Every one of the three elements is either included or excluded, giving 2³ = 8 subsets.

subject: discrete
title: An implication
prompt: When is the statement P → Q false?

options.text: When P is true and Q is false
When P and Q are both true
When P is false and Q is true

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An implication fails only when its premise holds but its conclusion does not.

subject: discrete
title: De Morgan’s law
prompt: Which expression is equivalent to ¬(P ∨ Q)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Negating a disjunction requires both alternatives to be false.

subject: discrete
title: Negating a quantified statement
prompt: What is the negation of “Every student passed”?

options.text: At least one student did not pass

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The negation of ∀x P(x) is ∃x ¬P(x).

subject: discrete
title: Ordered prizes
prompt: Five students compete for distinct gold, silver and bronze prizes. Nobody can receive two prizes. How many allocations are possible?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Choose the recipients in order: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

subject: discrete
title: Choosing a committee
prompt: How many committees of three can be chosen from six people?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Order does not matter, so choose 6! / (3!3!) = 20 committees.

subject: discrete
title: Repeated letters
prompt: How many distinct arrangements of the letters in LEVEL are possible?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The two Ls and two Es are indistinguishable: 5! / (2!2!) = 30.

subject: discrete
title: Two fair dice
prompt: Two independent fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that their sum is 7?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Six of the 36 equally likely ordered outcomes sum to 7.

subject: discrete
title: Without replacement
prompt: A bag has three red and two blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The probability is (3/5) × (2/4) = 3/10.

subject: discrete
title: Conditional probability
prompt: Suppose P(A ∩ B) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A | B)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: By definition P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B) = 0.2 / 0.5.

subject: discrete
title: Degrees and edges
prompt: An undirected graph has vertex degrees 1, 2, 2, 3, 4. How many edges does it have?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Each edge contributes two to the degree sum. The sum is 12, so there are 6 edges.

subject: discrete
title: Edges in a tree
prompt: A finite tree has 12 vertices. How many edges does it have?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A tree with n vertices has n − 1 edges.

subject: discrete
title: Bipartite cycles
prompt: Which cycle graph is not bipartite?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A graph is bipartite exactly when it has no odd cycle. A 5-cycle is odd.

subject: discrete
title: Greatest common divisor
prompt: What is gcd(84, 30)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Euclid’s algorithm gives 84 mod 30 = 24, 30 mod 24 = 6, and 24 mod 6 = 0.

subject: discrete
title: A modular inverse
prompt: What is the multiplicative inverse of 3 modulo 7?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam

subject: discrete
title: Simultaneous congruences
prompt: What is the smallest nonnegative integer x with x ≡ 1 (mod 3) and x ≡ 2 (mod 5)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The values 2, 7, 12, … satisfy the second congruence; 7 is the first also equal to 1 modulo 3.

subject: discrete
title: An equivalence relation
prompt: Which three properties define an equivalence relation?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Equivalence relations group elements into classes using reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity.

subject: discrete
title: Divisibility as an order
prompt: On the positive integers, the relation a R b iff a divides b is which type of relation?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Divisibility is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive; not every pair is comparable.

subject: discrete
title: Injective finite maps
prompt: How many injective functions are there from a 3-element set to a 5-element set?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Distinct inputs must map to distinct outputs: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

subject: discrete
title: Surjections onto two values
prompt: How many surjective functions are there from a 3-element set to a 2-element set?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: There are 2³ = 8 functions. Remove the two constant functions that omit one output.

subject: discrete
title: The pigeonhole principle
prompt: Thirteen people are assigned their birth month. What must be true?

options.text: At least three share a birth month
At least two share a birth month
Exactly two share a birth month

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Thirteen people occupy twelve month categories, so one category has at least two people.

subject: discrete
title: An induction step
prompt: In ordinary induction for a statement P(n), which implication is proved in the inductive step?

options.text: P(k) is false for every k
P(k) implies P(k + 1) for every allowed k

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: After the base case, the implication from each case to its successor propagates the result.

subject: discrete
title: A doubling recurrence
prompt: Let a₀ = 3 and aₙ = 2aₙ₋₁ for n ≥ 1. What is a₄?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Repeated doubling gives 3, 6, 12, 24, 48.

subject: discrete
title: A Fibonacci-type recurrence
prompt: Let a₀ = 0, a₁ = 1 and aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + aₙ₋₂. What is a₆?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The sequence begins 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8.

subject: discrete
title: A polynomial bound
prompt: What is the tight asymptotic order of 3n² + 7n + 4 as n grows?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The quadratic term dominates lower-degree terms and constant factors.

subject: discrete
title: Repeated halving
prompt: Starting with n = 2ᵏ, how many halvings are needed to reach 1?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: After j halvings the value is 2^(k−j), which equals 1 when j = k.

subject: discrete
title: Absorption
prompt: Which expression is equivalent to P ∨ (P ∧ Q)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: If P is true the expression is true; if P is false both terms are false.

subject: discrete
title: Eulerian circuits
prompt: A connected undirected graph with at least one edge has an Eulerian circuit exactly when what holds?

options.text: It has exactly two odd-degree vertices
Its number of vertices is even

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A closed trail using each edge once requires and, for a connected graph, is guaranteed by even degree at every vertex.
